name: Situational awareness
description: The adversary is constantly trying to understand its environment, its elements, and how it changes for effective decision-making.

subtechniques.name: Avoid blackmailing
subtechniques.description: The adversary is trying to prevent anyone from having the ability to blackmail him.

subtechniques.name: Avoid calling in the same room
subtechniques.description: Remove all phones, tablets and so on from the room where sensitive activities are conducted to avoid them issuing watermarked sounds as well as listening to keystroke sounds and watermarked sounds.

subtechniques.name: Avoid CCTV
subtechniques.description: Avoid CCTV in public places to prevent leaving a trail and the ability to get de-anonymized.

subtechniques.name: Avoid conducting sensitive activities from host OS
subtechniques.description: Host operating systems leak data which could be accessed more easily by forensic investigators. Using virtualization, especially combined with hidden volumes, makes it impossible to find any traces and thus contributes to plausible deniability.

subtechniques.name: Avoid cracked software
subtechniques.description: Cracked software often contains malware and should therefore be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid CSAM
subtechniques.description: Law enforcement agencies are all over CSAM hosters and users, avoiding CSAM might make you a less wanted person.

subtechniques.name: Avoid current device for shooting media
subtechniques.description:
Use only devices which haven’t been used to share media in the past, because camera fingerprints could contribute to de-anonymization.

subtechniques.name: Avoid discussing sensitive activities where lightbulbs could be seen from outside
subtechniques.description: Lightbulbs could be observed from a distance to listen to the sound in the room. Measures should be taken to prevent eavesdropping on sensitive information in rooms with lightbulbs.

subtechniques.name: Avoid discussing sensitive information in public
subtechniques.description: No-brainer.

subtechniques.name: Avoid drunkness/high
subtechniques.description: Loose lips might sink hips.

subtechniques.name: Avoid Google services
subtechniques.description: Avoid the use of Google Services by accessing the service through a public computer (if possible).

subtechniques.name: Avoid heavily monitored networks
subtechniques.description: Heavily monitored networks are unsuitable for sensitive operations and should therefore be avoided. Instead public Wi-Fi should be used.

subtechniques.name: Avoid host OS directly connecting to anything illegal
subtechniques.description: The host OS leaves trails locally which could be accessed more easily. Only conducting sensitive activities from virtual machines reduces the traces which are left and provides more control.

subtechniques.name: Avoid links
subtechniques.description: Links should never be trusted because they can be malicious or used in social engineering attacks. Avoiding them significantly reduces the possibility of malware infections or other incidents.

subtechniques.name: Avoid local area
subtechniques.description: For buying stuff anonymously, local area’s are avoided to prevent any links to your own identity and remain anonymous.

subtechniques.name: Avoid monitored systems and networks
subtechniques.description: Monitored systems and networks should be avoided for conducting sensitive activities, because there is a lack of control and can be seized without one’s permission.

subtechniques.name: Avoid peer-to-peer (P2P)
subtechniques.description: P2P services such as pirated software or torrents should be avoided as they could contain malware.

subtechniques.name: Avoid pluggin in untrusted devices
subtechniques.description: Never trust devices and avoid plugging them into equipment which is used for sensitive activities. Untrusted devices could contain malware and thus should be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid public places
subtechniques.description: For conducting sensitive activities, public crowded places should be avoided. Instead locations where no one can spy on you should be preferred.

subtechniques.name: Avoid risky platforms
subtechniques.description: Avoiding platforms which cooperate with law enforcement agencies or host content which is appropriate, since they draw more attention and could negatively impact you.

subtechniques.name: Avoid shortened links
subtechniques.description: Shortened links cannot be verified before redirection and should therefore never be trusted and thus avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid shoulder surfing
subtechniques.description:
If others could see what is happening on your screen this could expose sensitive information about you or your activities. To prevent this from happening, shoulder surfing should be avoided everywhere.

subtechniques.name: Avoid SMS authentication
subtechniques.description:
SMS authentication should be avoided because it is prone to SIM-swapping and Man-in-the-Middle attacks.

subtechniques.name: Avoid suspicious behavior
subtechniques.description:
Suspicious behavior could trigger human verifications, or reveal information which could be used against you. Such as OpSec guides on a decoy volume or anonymity or encryption software could make you suspicious just by using them.

subtechniques.name: Avoid unknown websites
subtechniques.description: Unknown websites should be avoided because they cannot be trusted.

subtechniques.name: Be very skeptical
subtechniques.description: Be very skeptical about everything by checking stuff twice before engaging with it.

subtechniques.name: Carry wallet in front pocket
subtechniques.description: Carrying a wallet in your front pocket makes it harder to steal unnoticed.

subtechniques.name: Copy and paste URL
subtechniques.description: URLs might be manually copied and pasted into the address bar and retyped to prevent typo squatting and homograph attacks.

subtechniques.name: Exclude exit nodes
subtechniques.description: Some Tor exit nodes might be excluded for example to match the fake identity’s location.

subtechniques.name: Fake IP geolocation should match fake identity
subtechniques.description: The fake IP geolocations might be adjusted to match their fake identities.

subtechniques.name: Keep low-profile
subtechniques.description: Keeping a low profile will draw less attention and may contribute to remaining anonymous.

subtechniques.name: Learn from OpSec mistakes
subtechniques.description: Cybercriminals who got arrested often make OpSec mistakes. Others are analyzing those and try to learn from them to prevent similar mistakes themselves.

subtechniques.name: Monitor for break-ins
subtechniques.description: Monitoring for break-ins could mean that something is stolen, tampered with, and so on, which requires immediate response.

subtechniques.name: Never bring personal phone when buying anonymously
subtechniques.description: Personal phones can be tracked, which could correlate your transaction back to you.

subtechniques.name: Never leave computer unattended
subtechniques.description: To prevent unauthorized access and tampering, devices should not be left unattended.

subtechniques.name: Paranoid mindset
subtechniques.description: To prevent OpSec mistakes, a paranoid mindset is required to doubt everything, trust nothing and verify everything.

subtechniques.name: Physical timing
subtechniques.description: For collecting packages or conducting physical transactions and meetings, timing should be taken into consideration. For example at night it is harder to recognize someone than during daytime.

subtechniques.name: Poisitioning devices
subtechniques.description: Devices and other sensitive stuff should be positioned in a way that no one can shoulder surf (from a distance).

subtechniques.name: Read developers documentation
subtechniques.description: Reading developers documentation helps to better understand how something works, which could help to preserve one’s security, privacy and anonymity.

subtechniques.name: Remove mobile devices from the room
subtechniques.description: Remove all phones, tablets and so on from the room to avoid them issuing watermakred sounds as well as listening to keystroke sounds and watermarked sounds.

subtechniques.name: Respond similarly
subtechniques.description: Whenever you receive a message from someone, responding in a similar way as they do mitigates stylometry attacks.

subtechniques.name: Travel by foot or bike
subtechniques.description: Public transport can leave a trail which should be avoided whenever possible.

subtechniques.name: Valid return address
subtechniques.description: To avoid attracting attention.

subtechniques.name: Verify domains
subtechniques.description: Domains might be verified before visiting them. Which could encompass OSINT-investigations.

subtechniques.name: Write lightly
subtechniques.description: To avoid leaving sensitive information when writing on a piece of paper, writing lightly could prevent the information being revealed from the page underneath.

subtechniques.name: Act if car GPS is being tracked
subtechniques.description: The adversary assumes that the GPS coordiates of his car are being tracked and acts accordingly.

subtechniques.name: Keep evidence minimal
subtechniques.description: The amount of evidence is minimized to reduce the associated risks.

subtechniques.name: Avoid saving customer addresses
subtechniques.description: The adversary is avoiding saving customer addresses because this might prove that he is a vendor.

subtechniques.name: Avoid roads with toll
subtechniques.description: Roads with toll might be avoided because they could leave traces behind about the individual.

subtechniques.name: Avoid cars with radio frequency communications
subtechniques.description: To prevent car movements from being tracked, cars with radio frequency communications might be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid Tor over Tor
subtechniques.description: Tor over Tor connections are avoided to prevent weaknesses.

subtechniques.name: Avoid using anonymously bought devices within CCTV storage window
subtechniques.description: CCTV is usually stored for 2-4 weeks. Avoid using anonymously bought equipment during that period prevents CCTV footage being traced back to you.

subtechniques.name: Read unsuccessful prosecutions
subtechniques.description: Unsuccessful cybercrime prosecutions might be read to understand how someone prevented going to jail.

subtechniques.name: Close and clean
subtechniques.description: Closing sessions and cleaning the browser (by shutting down), any traces of preveious sessions are wiped, such as cookies.

subtechniques.name: Avoid ignoring warnings
subtechniques.description: Warnings (e.g.  browser) are there for a reason, avoiding them might be harmful.

subtechniques.name: Avoid downloading from untrusted sources to prevent malware infections.
Show punycode
subtechniques.description: Enabling punycode in webbrowsers might contribute in detection of  phishing sites.

subtechniques.name: Awareness of law enforcement cryptocurrency lure technique
subtechniques.description: Law enforcement undercovers may approach vendors with scripted requests to conduct transactions in traceable cryptocurrencies (BTC) outside market infrastructure, using two documented social engineering pretexts: (1) claiming distrust of coin-swapping services; (2) claiming inability to perform coin swaps. The adversary recognises these patterns and maintains strict cryptocurrency discipline — refusing to transact outside established privacy-preserving payment infrastructure.
